chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who prayed two rakʿahs, then remembered in the second while he was in rukuʿ that he had left out one sajdah in the first.

He said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام used to say: If you leave out a sajdah in the first rakʿah and do not know whether it was one or two, then you begin again so that two valid rakʿahs are established for you. And if it is in the third and fourth, and you have left out a sajdah after having preserved the rukuʿ, then you repeat the sajdah.

key_terms.الثَّالِثَةِ: the third rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّابِعَةِ: the fourth rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.الرُّكُوعَ: the bowing position whose completion is legally consequential here
key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: being in the state of rukuʿ
key_terms.سَجْدَةً: a single sajdah omitted in prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets a sajdah in salat and only remembers after entering rukuʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets a sajdah during salat. It distinguishes between omission in the first rakʿah, where the prayer is restarted if the number is uncertain, and omission in the later rakʿahs after the rukuʿ has been preserved, where the sajdah is repeated.
